title: Khronos Corset -- the same stack with no emissive socket at all, which is what makes it the control

criterion.says: A female fabric mannequin with a corset and a collar.
criterion.note: THE ONE OF THE FOUR THAT DECLARES NO EMISSIVE SOCKET, and that is why it is here: with the emissive image bound, a slot whose material names none must render exactly as it did before, because glTF's emissiveFactor defaults to [0, 0, 0] and the white stand-in texel multiplies it to nothing. A case that only ever bound assets WITH an emissive image could not tell a correct binding from one that emits its stand-in. SUBJECT CLASS IS DERIVED: 0.11443452271378594 of 1280x720 = 105459 px^2 over 18324 triangles is 5.75 px^2 per triangle over both sides, about 2.9 px^2 on the side facing the camera -- so more than half of this subject's triangles are smaller than a pixel, which is the definition of sub-pixel-present.

acceptanceClass.because: A fronto-parallel planar placement owns three continuous freedoms -- two of aim and one of scale -- and every distinct silhouette line costs one condition, so 2 + k >= E is what decides whether the construction can be written at all (doc/requirements.md I.26.14). A curved fetched body of 18324 triangles resolves into thousands of distinct lines and no roll makes any of them rational; the acceptance is therefore worst_disagreement_px against the oracle's own filter half-width, which introduces no constant of its own.

subjects.name: Corset
subjects.notes: The binary spelling, so the images travel inside the one file the store is keyed on. A SUPPLIED TANGENT, which is the half of the normal-map question our generator never reaches: `Subject` must not regenerate one, and this asset is where a real exporter's basis crosses.

source.pinReason: the corpus's single pin; every Khronos subject in the tree is read at this commit so that one bump moves all of them

blender.note: A release version, not a commit. Recorded so a red rung can be attributed to our renderer or to the oracle, and carried in the oracle's cache key so a version bump misses instead of serving a stale render. We do not aim to be bit-identical with Cycles.

camera.derivation: The framing rule of doc/requirements.md I.26.10 (src/gltf/Framing.h) applied to this subject's own bounds and to nothing else: azimuth 35 deg and elevation 20 deg in glTF's +Y-up frame, distance r / sin(yfov/2) / 0.6 about the AABB's centre, yfov = 2*atan(12/50) from Blender's factory 50 mm lens on a 24 mm sensor height at sensor_fit VERTICAL, near = distance - r and far = distance + r. THE ROLL IS ZERO AND STATED: this subject's silhouette is not rational at any roll, so a roll would be a different draw of the same lottery rather than an exactness argument.
camera.note: The file carries no camera, so this case's camera is declared here and the oracle builds the same one from these numbers.

light.note:
A DELTA LIGHT AND NOT AN ENVIRONMENT, and on a metal-rough asset that is what makes the row decidable at all: a uniform environment delivers the same radiance from every direction, so roughness, metalness and the normal map all stop changing the picture. IRRADIANCE pi W/m^2 IS DERIVED AND NOT CHOSEN: a Lambertian white facet facing the beam returns rho*E/pi = 1, so the picture is scene-referred around unity and no exposure decides whether it is legible. THE ANGULAR DIAMETER IS ZERO AND THE RUNNER REFUSES ANYTHING ELSE -- a sun with an angle is a disc, which is an area source, an estimator in the oracle and a soft terminator no punctual light draws. THE BEAM IS SLANTED OFF THE VIEW AXIS -- the framing rule puts the eye at azimuth 35 deg and elevation 20 deg, and a light down the same axis is a headlight that flattens every form the row is supposed to shape.

ESTIMATOR: FILTER-SAMPLE, AND IT IS THE MEASUREMENT THAT SAYS SO RATHER THAN THE DECLARATION. This subject declares no emissive socket, so its own surface is not a second source and `selected` would be the wrong word; but the two seeds still disagree on 107 of 2 764 800 colour samples over 39 pixels, at a relative 1.1e-07 median and 2.71e-07 worst, with NO sample binary and NO pixel touching a coverage boundary. Cycles was checked bit-reproducible run to run at a fixed seed, so the seed is the whole of it, and at 1 spp the only thing the seed still moves is where inside the pixel the single camera ray goes. A dense curved body's shading varies across that footprint and a flat plate's does not, which is why `NormalTangentTest` is `delta` under the same recipe and this is not.

world.note: BLACK, AND THAT IS THE REDUCTION RATHER THAN A LOOK. Blender's factory world is an area source Cycles samples, which at one sample per pixel is a Bernoulli draw rather than a value. With the world at zero the only source left is a light with no area, the estimator has no variance, and the two seeds must agree bit for bit.

material.note:
THE FILE'S OWN ROW ENTIRE, and it has to be: the subject IS the material stack, and every arm that LOWERS the closure -- a diffuse or an emissive one -- throws away everything but one image. The file states base colour, metallic-roughness and normal in three images and this arm binds all three; it declares no emissive socket at all, which is why it is here -- it is the control for the three assets beside it that do.

WHAT THE ORACLE HAS AND WE DO NOT IS VISIBILITY. Cycles traces a shadow ray per shading event, so its render of this asset carries the body's own shadow; `render/stages/SubjectDraw.h` states in its own words that neither arm computes visibility, so ours does not. THAT DIFFERENCE IS IN THE PICTURE AND IT IS NOT A TOLERANCE: this case is `self-describing`, the image residual is printed and decides nothing, and what is judged is the placement exactly and the appearance by eye.

default.note: One sample per pixel with the box filter at its RNA minimum makes Cycles evaluate the same coverage predicate a centre-sampling rasteriser does. The only source is a light with no area over a world of strength zero, so the estimator has no variance left and the two seeds must agree bit for bit.

subjectFrameFraction.derivation: the sum over the subject's 18324 triangles of the magnitude of the projected signed area, over 1280*720 at the declared camera, recomputed by the runner from the fetched vertices
subjectFrameFraction.note: An AREA and not a coverage: every triangle counts by the magnitude of its signed area, so a closed body counts its far side too and this number is about twice the silhouette.
